items.reason: Line 9: #define ADC_FULL 4095.0f /* 12-bit converter */. Used as the ADC full-scale count for scaling (as the denominator in K_VS).
Line 10: #define DAC_FULL 4095 /* comparator reference DAC */. Full-scale DAC code used to form comparator DAC thresholds (CMP_DAC_LO uses DAC_FULL).
Line 13: #define VBUS_FS 498.3f /* V at ADC full scale */ for the DC bus ADC sense chain; this directly matches vbus_fs (divider ratio × ADC reference).
Line 14: #define K_VS (VBUS_FS / ADC_FULL) /* V per count */. This computes volts-per-ADC-count and corresponds to vbus_scale.
Line 17: #define VBAT_FS 168.0f /* V at ADC full scale */ for the battery ADC sense chain; corresponds to vbat_fs.
Line 20: #define VO_FS_PK 501.6f /* peak V at +/- half scale */ for the mid-rail-biased output-voltage sense range; corresponds to vout_fs_pk.
Line 23: #define IO_FS_PK 33.0f /* peak A at +/- half scale */ for the mid-rail-biased output-current sense range; corresponds to iout_fs_pk.
Line 24: #define CMP_DAC_HI 3364 /* positive overcurrent trip code */. This is the positive hardware peak-current comparator DAC code; matches iout_pklim_dac_hi.
Line 25: #define CMP_DAC_LO (DAC_FULL - CMP_DAC_HI) /* negative overcurrent trip code */. Computed negative threshold DAC code; corresponds to iout_pklim_dac_lo.
FW_VER_MAJ (line 19) defines the firmware major version; literal 2 is used as an identifier, not a physical quantity.
VIN_LO_XFER (line 22) is the AC input window lower transfer point: “go to battery below this, Vrms”; literal 85.0f volts RMS.
VIN_HI_XFER (line 23) is the AC input window upper transfer point: “go to battery above this, Vrms”; literal 265.0f volts RMS.

VBUS_REF (line 26) is labeled “PFC regulation target, V” with value 400.0f. This is a bus setpoint, but the spec rule vbus_set requires the rule’s “minimum plus design margin, rounded up to 10 V” criterion, which is not explicitly shown here.
VO_NOM (line 29) is “output, Vrms”; literal 220.0f RMS output voltage setpoint.
VO_TOL (line 30) defines the regulation band tolerance “+/- regulation band” as +/-0.03. It is a band-width parameter used to derive VO_HI/VO_LO, not itself a band edge or directly a spec rule level.
VO_HI (line 31) computes the upper edge of the regulation band as (VO_NOM * (1.0f + VO_TOL)). By construction it is vout_hi; expression is derived from VO_NOM and VO_TOL.
IO_RATED (line 32) is “A rms” with value 12.5f; this is the rated output current (RMS).
I_TRIP_RMS (line 33) is “overload shutdown, A rms”; literal 14.0f. This matches the software overload trip level concept.
TMR_LD (line 36) is “PWM period, 25 kHz carrier” with literal 6000; used as the PWM period register value in counts.
DB_CNT (line 37) is “300 us dead time” with literal 30; categorically this is the dead-time register value in counts.
K_P (line 40) is the voltage loop proportional gain with literal 0.8f.
K_I (line 41) is the voltage loop integral gain “per control ISR” with literal 0.015f; this corresponds to vloop_ki.
VBAT_NOM (line 44) is “string nominal, V” with literal 89.6f, matching vbat_nom.
VBAT_CUT (line 45) is “end of discharge” with literal 78.4f; corresponds to low-battery shutdown (vbat_cutoff).
UART_BAUD (line 48) defines “front-panel / RS-232 port” baud rate; literal 19200. No spec rule id corresponds to UART baud.
PIN_BYP_RELAY (line 49) is “GPIO, static bypass relay drive” with literal 12; a GPIO pin assignment, not a spec-rule-mappable physical threshold.
FLT_LOG_LEN=16 defines the fault log ring buffer length (flt_log size) used by log_fault via flt_idx++ & (FLT_LOG_LEN - 1).
k_trip_a=15.0f is the software overload trip RMS threshold used in prot_slow: if (i_rms > k_trip_a) then increment ol_ms and eventually inv_off/log FLT_OL after a hold time.

ol_hold_ms=5000 is the overload ride-through/hold time used in prot_slow: when ++ol_ms >= ol_hold_ms the code turns off and logs FLT_OL. ol_ms is described as being incremented on the slow (1 ms) path.

21.2f in prot_fast: if (a > 21.2f) where a is |i_pk|, then inv_off and log FLT_OC. It is annotated as 'peak of the RMS trip level' and acts as a fast per-cycle overcurrent protection trip (peak hardware-like action), but it is not explicitly a comparator DAC code; mapped to iout_pk_limit by function.
0.9f in prot_slow: if (vo_rms < 0.9f * VO_NOM) log FLT_BRN. This constant sets the undervoltage brightness threshold as 90% of VO_NOM; it is a ratio multiplier, not an absolute voltage constant.
3 in prot_restart: if (retry < 3) then delay_ms(500), retry++, inv_on(). It is a maximum restart attempt count (retry limit), not a regulated quantity.
500 in prot_restart is the restart delay time passed to delay_ms(500) before inv_on() on each retry attempt.
